sources.title: Gigabit Infrastructure Subsidy Scheme guidance: clawback
facts: Clawback recovers excess subsidy where a beneficiary has been over-compensated.
Planning and build true-up, active services and passive services are monitored separately.
Supplier take-up reporting can trigger retrospective subsidy adjustment.
The monitoring and clawback period is at least seven years after completion of the contracted build.
Financial-control status is not evidence that a network is live at a specific address.

sources.title: Public Review and National Rolling OMR Disagreement Resolution Process
facts: The process concerns disagreements over subsidy-control determinations from Public Review and National Rolling OMR.
The NCC must remain functionally separate from procurement delivery teams for its assessment role.
The process covers Gigabit-white and under-review determinations, not every aspect of intervention-area formation.
Invitations to Tender should not issue while a material disagreement remains unresolved.
A disputed classification remains administrative evidence and not current service proof.

sources.title: GIS Worked Example: Assessment Form for Gigabit Capable Solutions
facts: The form gathers technical and commercial evidence supporting gigabit or ultrafast capability claims.
Subsidised infrastructure must offer significant new capability rather than minor upgrades.
Gigabit capability requires connections capable of 1 Gbit/s download and 200 Mbit/s upload without future hardware changes.
The example is explicitly illustrative and must be replaced with specific operational evidence in real submissions.
A technology-capability assessment is not a verified record of service at every claimed premise.

sources.title: Access to Infrastructure Code – Use of Existing Infrastructure
facts: GIS suppliers must comply with the code or confirm they hold no relevant infrastructure in the intervention area.
Access to physical infrastructure should be offered on fair and reasonable terms unless refusal is objectively justified.
Requested information can include mast and pole points, duct routes, available capacity and rental costs.
Information-request response periods vary according to whether advance interest was declared.
Infrastructure-access records support procurement and do not prove broadband service at an address.

sources.title: Project Gigabit procurement pipeline
facts: The subsidy-advice collection publishes a separate ODS procurement-pipeline file.
The collection was last updated on 26 July 2024 and records an ODS pipeline revision dated 18 December 2023.
The pipeline belongs to the subsidy-control and procurement evidence family.
Procurement status must remain distinct from contracted, built and live-service status.
A pipeline entry cannot be promoted to parcel truth without delivery and exact-premises evidence.

sources.title: Connectivity and Accessibility supplementary data tables, July 2026
sources.lines: document list and July 2026 release details
facts: The July 2026 digest updates broadband and mobile-coverage analysis for rural and urban England.
Supplementary tables provide statistics by Rural-Urban Classification.
The tables are a separate downloadable evidence object from the narrative digest.
Classification, denominator and observation date must be retained when producing rural comparisons.
Rural aggregate statistics do not establish availability for an individual property.

sources.title: Connectivity and Accessibility local authority data tables, July 2026
facts: The release provides local-authority datasets used in the rural connectivity analysis where feasible.
Local-authority tables are disaggregated supporting data rather than parcel records.
Broadband and mobile indicators have different units and coverage concepts.
Local-authority boundaries and Rural-Urban Classification categories must be preserved.
Area statistics require an exact UPRN join before any parcel-level promotion.

sources.title: Superfast Broadband Programme Evaluation: Key Benefits and Impacts
facts: The evaluation covers economic, social, environmental and market impacts of the Superfast Broadband Programme.
The programme was established because commercial deployment was expected to miss some areas.
BDUK is the accountable programme body.
Evaluation outputs assess additionality and value for money at programme or area level.
Historic impact evidence is contextual and not current service proof.

sources.title: Local Full Fibre Network Evaluation Plan
facts: The plan evaluates waves two and three of the Local Full Fibre Networks programme.
The programme was a £200 million intervention intended to stimulate commercial investment.
The plan uses phased work packages and multiple evaluation methods.
The evaluation seeks lessons relevant to future digital-infrastructure initiatives.
Evaluation design and historic programme effects are not current parcel availability.

sources.title: BDUK Vouchers Evaluation: Impacts and Value for Money Assessment
facts: The evaluation examines vouchers issued and connected by March 2021.
It combines counterfactual coverage analysis, economic analysis and beneficiary surveys.
It includes wellbeing, environmental and initial cost-benefit assessment components.
Evaluated historical connections have a different vintage from current coverage data.
Programme additionality estimates cannot be reused as exact present-day parcel observations.
